title: Linear and Quadratic Functions: y = mx + c and y = ax² + q
seo_title: Grade 10 Linear and Quadratic Functions Worksheets with Answers (CAPS Maths)
standard_text: Investigate the effect of a and q on the graphs of y = ax + q and y = ax² + q; find the domain, range, intercepts with the axes, turning points and axes of symmetry; sketch graphs and find their equations.
meta_desc: Free CAPS Grade 10 worksheets: linear graphs y = mx + c and parabolas y = ax² + q, turning points, range, intercepts and equations. 100 questions with memos.
key_big: TP of y = ax² + q is (0; q).
body_html:
How to think about it

  • y = mx + c: m is the gradient and c is the y-intercept.
  • y = ax² + q: a > 0 gives ∪ (minimum), a < 0 gives ∩ (maximum).
  • The turning point of y = ax² + q is (0; q), and the range is y ≥ q or y ≤ q.
  • x-intercepts: put y = 0 and solve.

Examples

Example

y = 2x² − 8

TP (0; −8)

0 = 2x² − 8, x² = 4

Answer: x = ±2

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
m or cm multiplies x.
(q; 0)The turning point is (0; q).
Only +x² = 4 gives x = ±2.

items.q: What is the gradient of the line y = −4x?
items.e: In y = mx + c, the gradient is the number in front of x: −4.

items.q: What is the gradient of the line y = −5 − 4x?
items.e: Write it as y = −4x + −5: the gradient is −4.

items.e: Write it as y = −4x + −1: the gradient is −4.

items.q: Find the gradient of the line through (3; −3) and (7; −5).
items.e: Gradient = change in y ÷ change in x = (−5 − (−3)) ÷ (7 − 3) = −2 ÷ 4 = −12.

items.q: Find the gradient of the line through (1; 13) and (−3; 5).
items.e: Gradient = change in y ÷ change in x = (5 − 13) ÷ (−3 − 1) = −8 ÷ −4 = 2.

items.q: Find the gradient of the line through (5; 0) and (1; −4).
items.e: Gradient = change in y ÷ change in x = (−4 − 0) ÷ (1 − 5) = −4 ÷ −4 = 1.

items.q: Find the gradient of the line through (1; −3) and (−1; −2).
items.e: Gradient = change in y ÷ change in x = (−2 − (−3)) ÷ (−1 − 1) = 1 ÷ −2 = −12.

items.q: Find the gradient of the line through (3; −10) and (−1; −2).
items.e: Gradient = change in y ÷ change in x = (−2 − (−10)) ÷ (−1 − 3) = 8 ÷ −4 = −2.

items.q: What is the equation of the line?
items.e: It crosses the y-axis at 2, so c = 2. For every 1 across it goes down 2, so m = −2. y = −2x + 2.

items.q: What is the equation of the line?
items.e: It crosses the y-axis at −3, so c = −3. For every 1 across it goes up 2, so m = 2. y = 2x − 3.

items.q: What is the equation of the line?
items.e: It crosses the y-axis at 3, so c = 3. For every 1 across it goes down 3, so m = −3. y = −3x + 3.

items.q: What is the equation of the line?
items.e: It crosses the y-axis at −2, so c = −2. For every 1 across it goes up 1, so m = 1. y = x − 2.

items.q: What is the equation of the line?
items.e: It crosses the y-axis at −1, so c = −1. It is horizontal, so y = −1.
